Q: Easygui isn't installing A:

First make sure your Python, which you want to download meets requirements of Easygui, then when installing select Add to path option. After installing:

If Windows:

  1. Open CMD
  2. Type pip install easygui or python -m pip install easygui

If Linux:

  1. Open your terminal

  2. Type pip install easygui or python3 -m pip install easygui

Q: Correct way to represent a while loop with one task in BPMN? A:

Both approaches are valid BPMN. They just communicate differently.

Gateway loop (explicit):

This is technically a do-while (task runs at least once, then checks). If you want a proper while (check first, then maybe run the task), flip it: put the condition gateway before the task.

Good when you need the loop logic to be visible in the diagram. Business people can look at it and understand "ah, it keeps retrying until X."

Loop marker on the task (compact):

Start → [ Task ↻ ] → End

The little circular arrow at the bottom of the task. You set loopCondition, testBefore (true = while, false = do-while), and optionally loopMaximum in the task properties.

Same semantics, just hides the details. Good for technical diagrams or well-understood patterns like "retry 3 times" or "poll until response."

Which to pick? Depends on your audience. If the loop condition matters to the reader, use the gateway. If the loop is just an implementation detail (retries, polling), use the marker. Don't use both for the same loop.

One more thing: if there's complex logic inside the loop (multiple tasks, branching), wrap it in a sub-process and put the loop marker on that instead.

Disclosure: I teach the BPMN 2.0 Master Class on Udemy (40k+ students). For quick reference on these elements, see Exclusive Gateway and Sub-Process.

Q: How to get document_topics distribution of all of the document in gensim LDA? A:

The function get_document_topics takes an input of a single document in BOW format. You're calling it on the full corpus (an array of documents) so it returns an iterable object with the scores for each document.

You have a few options. If you just want one document, run it on the document you want the values for:

document_topics = model.get_document_topics(corpus[0])

or do the following to get an array of scores for all the documents:

document_topics = [model.get_document_topics(item) for item in corpus]

Or directly access each object from your original code:

document_topics = model.get_document_topics(corpus)
print(get_document_topics[0])

Q: Unable to redirect after login in React app using AWS Cognito A:

In this case, there's no need to define getSession, authenticate and logout on the context. You can put those functions inside a auth folder and call them whenever you need wihout having to define them in the context. What you need to define in the context is whether the user is logged in or not, because that's the information that you want to share in your whole application. Regarding the AccountContext is not defined, I don't see any issues from what you have shared. https://codesandbox.io/s/adoring-sun-kz30yr?file=/src/Settings.js
